sources.text: # DecentBusking **Drop a track. Join the loop. Mint it when you’re ready.** DecentBusking is a community listening room, a 3D timeline of music NFTs, and a Discord radio built around the people who make the music. Listen, explore the archive, tip a performer, or bring a track into JukeLoop. Between tracks, the radio's waiting or up-next message uses the song-title ticker. On mobile, compact votes are centered between Discord and the watchlist eyes; compact audio controls sit between the hat and briefcase above the ad countdown. These shared rows keep the footer small. Watchlist eyes mirror the Discord icon on mobile only. Desktop keeps the radio player centered, Discord beside the hat, and the watchlist button immediately after the vote count. The eyes save verified NFTs to your watchlist; their accessible label describes the current save state. The next-ad countdown is centered at the bottom on mobile and stays in the player on desktop. Read the [Decent Busking whitepaper](WHITEPAPER.md) for the vision, current architecture, payment mechanics, artist-rights limits, and roadmap. Implemented features are separated from future plans. ## v1.0.0 Supporter release Approved release terms: **100 editions at 100 Base USDC each**, with a 10% ERC-2981 royalty signal to `thejollylama.eth` (not universally enforced). Preparation archives and pins the exact release commit, runnable site, front/back artwork and metadata. It does not mint, transfer stock, list or update ENS. The steward reviews each wallet signature: mint to the resolved creator wallet, then deposit/list in the existing shared escrow. Primary proceeds stay in that owner-controlled escrow until withdrawn; the royalty recipient does not redirect primary sales. The target is `decentbusking.decentagency.eth`. Its Ethereum controller must sign the fresh contenthash update and the result must serve the pinned site. About keeps its explicit preparation state until verified Base purchase evidence exists. [Issue #73](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentBusking/issues/73) remains the acceptance gate for mint, ownership/supply/royalties, purchase path and announcement. The existing escrow's MetaMask/Blockaid false-positive review is pending; this release neither claims clearance nor disables wallet warnings. Reuse: the shared [DecentHead product kit at `409fa9d`](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentHead/tree/409fa9decd22715c94b827455bede7d43cc884dc) binds quantity and six-decimal price across artwork, metadata, listing verification and announcements. Matching Market studio and Office checkout support 100 USDC without changing historical 10-USDC editions. This release uses current main's integrated collaborator/tutorial work; the older dirty development checkout is preserved separately, not copied over newer shipped functionality.

## Come Listen The **DJuke** drawer uses a chrome/platinum jukebox with an animated quarter, music notes and a dim LCD equalizer driven by the shared live music spectrum. DVert uses the same meter behind its prices and animates its tab icons in the header. Meters rest without playback and stop when hidden or reduced motion is enabled; no independent media sources or simulated music loops are created. Its **i** button explains queue pricing, payment splits and worker-gas charges. Connect through the page header; a disconnected **Queue Song** click shows the wallet reminder without starting a transaction. DJuke supports a profile-backed playlist draft and signed, immutable playlist library. Named playlists are 1–10 distinct songs at a flat 0.25 USDC/song; private playback never changes the existing creator-priced listen path. Radio checkout remains disabled until a compatible contract and batch-aware worker are separately reviewed and configured. See [playlist pricing, fees, signatures and rollout decisions](docs/DJUKE-PLAYLISTS.md). **Top Jukebox Earners** ranks the top three artist/collaborator wallets by all-time confirmed DJuke song-play payouts, with ENS or decorated wallet links to Basescan. It reuses the checkpointed earnings index at `GET /api/djuke/earners`, excluding album purchases, withdrawals, listener spending and platform payouts. Unavailable/incomplete indexing is reported explicitly, not shown as zero earnings. Deploy both the worker and site for this feature. All DJuke decorative animations respect reduced-motion preferences. The **Top 10** title also has an **i** dialog explaining net votes, weekly prize estimates and closeout, Friday Hype's opening chart, and playlist saves. Voting with the radio thumbs-up/down buttons keeps the chart open. Confirmed votes refresh its counts and rankings immediately; other listeners' votes are picked up by the existing 15-second refresh while the panel is open. While a song or advert plays, a dim live meter stays above the first visible chart row, rising behind the panel's title and subtitle without covering their controls, even when the playing song is ranked farther down the chart. The upper-left meter button switches between frequency bars and the actual time-domain waveform, using the radio's shared analyser. The filled waveform uses reduced amplitude, averaged samples and rounded curves for a gentler look. The meter rests without playback and stops for reduced motion. While a main-radio advert plays, an unranked **Advert · Live Now** row shows its per-play net votes and uses the same live bar/wave meter. The vote tooltip gives up/down counts. It disappears on song handoff, has no playlist-save control, and never participates in music rankings or prize calculations. Counts require the matching worker update; older workers show unavailable rather than zero. **First visit?** Follow the [newcomer walkthrough](docs/NEWCOMERS.md) for a click-by-click listener and artist route with screenshots. The on-site **Follow the white rabbit** launcher appears front and center in the main scene on mobile and desktop until the tour is dismissed or completed. An

incomplete tour automatically resumes on refresh at the furthest card reached,
including its playlist hop; going Back does not reduce saved progress. Viewing
every card completes the tour, so later refreshes keep it hidden. Progress and
completion are remembered in that browser, using local storage.
The playlist-only deep-link guide remembers its own furthest hop and completion
without marking the rest of onboarding complete.
The identical rabbit button remains
available in the DBusker About modal for replay. The Mercury symbol follows the white rabbit with
musical accessories and a small flying-money icon, while the rabbit mascot peeks
in and out of holes beside highlighted controls. Factual text explains each stop;
Mercury is a visual companion, not a narrator. This
read-only guided tour opens real drawers and ankh menus; it never triggers wallet,
vote, upload, purchase, or audio actions. Exit restores existing drawers and visible
briefcase drafts. The tutorial stays open while visitors click or keyboard-navigate
the highlighted site features on mobile and desktop. Outside clicks do not
dismiss it; **Escape**, **Close tutorial** (X), or **Leave tour** hide the card,
buttons, bunny, and center launcher until refresh. About remains available for
explicit replay, including after completion. A completed tour does not auto-open
even if the URL still contains `?tutorial=playlists`.
Active submissions, open dialogs, and VertLoop listening defer
the tour with an explanation. Keyboard navigation, focus return, narrow screens,
and reduced-motion preferences are supported.

The subheader's **Search Artist or Song** field searches the indexed music
catalog by artist or title. It shares its query with archive search; typing in
the subheader clears any archive artist selection so a new search covers all
artists. The archive retains its separate artist dropdown and result counts.
The footer shows live net votes beside the thumbs: songs use the current New York
weekly chart total; adverts use votes for the current advert play. Totals refresh
with the radio poll and after a confirmed vote. Unavailable totals show a dash,
not a guessed zero.
The tilted block-style counter celebrates actual increases with floating music
notes and sinks toward a hole on decreases. Initial loads and track changes do
not trigger vote celebrations; reduced-motion preferences disable the effects.
Header menu coins accept clicks across their full coin area and support Enter
and Space. The warm orange-white neon title flickers briefly every 30 seconds;
the end symbols carry a travelling electric pulse. Both remain steady with
reduced motion enabled.

The footer uses a compact advert countdown: “next ad after this song”, “next ad
after next song”, or “next ad after N more songs”, without changing scheduling.
Footer NFT verification matches the exact IPFS media identity even when radio
playback uses a relay or preloaded blob URL. Lookup failures report verification
unavailability rather than implying the song has not been minted.

Open the [DecentBusking town square](https://thejollylama.github.io/DecentBusking/) and explore the 3D music timeline. Select a track in the archive to click **Preview** for a free 30-second taste or **Listen** to play the whole song, inspect its NFT details, and tip the artist. Connect MetaMask on Base when you want to send a tip.

The site radio streams and preloads recordings through the worker's public `GET /api/radio/media?cid=…` endpoint, which only serves recordings known to the radio playlist. The worker uses its dedicated IPFS gateway (or the original Discord upload) without sharing gateway credentials with browsers, and forwards HTTP ranges for seeking. The configured public gateway remains a browser fallback. Deploy both the worker and site when updating this route.

The portable radio scopes asynchronous `play()` results to each loaded recording.
A delayed rejection from replaced media cannot pause or clear the next track.

The site distinguishes explicit decoder failures from gateway/network failures.
Unsupported recordings are not automatically retried during the same radio play;
decoder diagnostics stay in the console rather than displaying a listener warning,
and the player attempts the next song normally. Temporary media-load failures try the fallback gateway, then
retry the play after at least 15 and 30 seconds (three attempts total).
Load diagnostics include the URL and browser media error in the console. This
does not transcode recordings: the worker currently serves their original codec,
which some embedded browsers cannot decode even when the file is available.

On mobile (up to 600px), camera buttons are hidden; use the 3D scene's touch
gestures to orbit, pinch to zoom, and pan with two fingers. Timeline navigation
remains available, and desktop camera buttons are unchanged.
The mobile timeline uses a single row, side tabs are shortened, and drawers
keep only a small clearance above the measured footer. Empty footer action and
watchlist-status rows do not reserve space.

Join [DecentBusking on Discord](https://discord.gg/SCtcBggHPa), head to **#DecentJukebox**, and tune in to the **JukeLoop** voice channel. The radio rotates community uploads; listeners can react 👍 or 👎. The bot tracks cumulative votes and plays, and the ratings influence future rotation.

Open the **Top 10** pull-tab on the upper-left to see this New York week's most-voted songs and their current USDC prize estimates. Each song holds its own prize place, even when one artist has several winning songs. First place receives half the weekly pot, each subsequent place receives half the remaining pot, and the last payable place receives the remainder. Every payable prize must exceed $0.10; a smaller pot supports fewer payable places. A song without a linked artist wallet by Monday midnight forfeits its assigned prize without redistributing it; the amount stays in the Top10 fund for the next week. The chart greys out that prize and warns the musician to register a wallet ASAP. Estimates change with votes and confirmed funding, then freeze at Monday midnight in America/New_York. Payments still require owner approval.

The **Top10 fund** and **Playback fund** buttons open the current prize pool, pending estimates, confirmed activity, and weekly payout archive. The small **i** beside each fund panel title explains pending and frozen payments. DVert funding entries include the purchaser's ENS name or wallet, recovered from the confirmed campaign purchase event. Wallet labels fall back to maintainer-registered names in `contributor-accounts.json` when no verified ENS name is available; contract sources, including the DVert paid queue, link to their named BaseScan code pages. The pool uses the latest fund balance with the weekly reservation and allocation policy, rather than replacing it with an older weekly balance snapshot. Deploy both the site and worker for these purchaser details.

Friday's **Top 10 Hype Hour** (8-9 p.m. America/New_York by default) plays a checkpointed opening chart from its lowest place toward opening #1. Votes keep changing the live chart, not that show's play order. The festival sidepanel pops out when the hour starts (it can be minimized while the countdown keeps playing), the radio player shows **Listening to Top 10 Friday Night Hype**, the panel's **i** button explains the program, labels opening and live ranks separately, and offers **+** buttons to save verified songs to your personal playlist (your wallet-backed profile watchlist). During Hype only, the expanded panel can cover the header/footer: desktop places the scrollable chart beside the festival poster, while mobile stacks them with room for at least four to five songs on typical phone screens. Outside Hype, the regular drawer size and header/footer clearance are unchanged. Signing a watchlist save is not a purchase. Early finishes use labelled encores of the same opening selection; the scheduled handoff still takes priority at 9 p.m., even if the countdown is unfinished.

### Announcing a radio hour to Discord (owner only)

Open **Admin → Radio Programming**, refresh the shared calendar, and check one
**dated occurrence** under **Promote a radio-hour occurrence**. This covers Top10,
live blocks, other playlist hours, and one-off shows; selecting a recurring show
never promotes its entire series. Checking/unchecking only selects — it never
posts. Edit the reason to tune in, select mention targets, click **Preview
announcement**, then **Confirm — send to Discord** and sign with the owner wallet.

The preview names the server-configured destination (default **#themessagebox**,
`943117480883265539`) and includes New York date/time, Discord-localized times,
and website/voice listening links. **@everyone is selected by default**; uncheck
it and select mentionable guild roles (such as JukeboxHero), or uncheck everything
for no mentions. Operators can change the default with `ANNOUNCE_DEFAULT_MENTION`.

After delivery the panel shows the Discord message link and last-announced time.
Retries do not create a second post; a deliberate repeat requires checking
**Intentionally re-announce** and making a new preview/confirmation.

Schedule changes, cancellations, ended/removed occurrences, missing permissions,
and storage/Discord failures are rejected visibly. Refresh and preview/reconfirm
changed events. An uncertain delivery is reconciled rather than blindly resent;
see [bot operator instructions](discord-bot/README.md#manual-calendar-announcements).
Public calendars have no promotion controls. This does not change playback or
start-of-show announcements, create Discord Scheduled Events, or send reminders.

### Cancelling a live slot

Open the community radio schedule with the owner wallet connected and choose **Cancel event** on the dated occurrence. Enter a public reason, confirm, and sign the calendar update. The occurrence remains visible with a red **Canceled** stamp for seven days; future recurring Fridays are unchanged. The shared worker calendar persists the cancellation across restarts, and open calendars refresh every 15 seconds. Cancellation does not approve, refund, or settle performer payments.

Listeners can choose **Set reminder** for the next weekly show or a scheduled
live event. Apple/Outlook `.ics` downloads include a 15-minute display alarm.
Google Calendar opens a prefilled event; select a 15-minute notification before
saving (Google's event-template URL does not set notification preferences).
Save into an account synced across devices; imported individual events do not
receive later schedule updates.

**Sync the community radio calendar** exposes the public
`GET /api/radio/calendar.ics` subscription for Google, Apple and Outlook.
The feed includes weekly shows and live bookings for the next 90 days plus
seven days of recent occurrences. It uses stable occurrence UIDs, UTC timestamps
calculated from New York wall-clock times (including DST), cancellation status
and 15-minute alarms. Calendar clients control refresh frequency and whether
subscription alarms are enabled; updates are not instant. During calendar
restore the endpoint returns 503 rather than an incomplete feed that could
remove subscribers' events. No wallet, notification permission or personal
calendar credentials are needed by DecentBusking.

Cancelled live slots leave automated radio running. After Friday Hype, or when starting in a cancelled live slot, the radio tries an eligible advert before returning to music, subject to existing campaign capacity, availability, and paid-request priority. Never-played campaigns get preference in ordinary main-radio advert selection; paid priority boosts remain ahead of that preference.

**DVert campaigns cost $5 USDC for one week.** To run an ended advert again, open **My Ads**, select the minted ad, check its name under **Run Campaign**, choose weeks, and press **Purchase Campaign**. The upload draft in **Submit Ad** is separate; you do not need to upload or mint the advert again. Checkout displays selection, network, availability, and payment progress messages. Optional priority payments do not buy or extend a campaign. A **queue bump** starts at $1 USDC, doubling every seven pending requests, and moves an active approved advert to the next normal advert break. **Play after this song** costs **2x that queue price** for an extra break. Immediate requests take priority over bumps, FIFO is preserved within each tier, and both defer during protected shows. Payments remain reserved until naturally completed playback; removed unplayed requests have payer-claimed full refunds. Checkout pauses when the required local checkpoint mirror or main radio is offline; existing payments remain queued and retry when service returns. The next-ad notice identifies paid requests and any delay. The replacement two-tier contract is deployed and source verified; a real $2 immediate request was recovered, played and settled into all four funds on 2026-10-19. Deploy the updated worker and static site together for availability gating and paid notices. See the [paid advert queue policy and deployment checklist](docs/DVERT-PAID-QUEUE.md).

### Songs Awaiting Your Vote — one-off playlist hours

The owner can schedule **Songs Awaiting Your Vote** in **Admin → Radio Programming**:
choose **Playlist show**, keep the reusable **Songs Awaiting Your Vote — no votes ever**
definition, enter the title and New York start/end dates, review the rule/count/duration
preview, then **Schedule event** and authorize the calendar update with the owner wallet.
For tonight, **Thursday October 22, 2026**, use **2026-10-22 21:00 → 22:00**
(America/New_York; stored as **2026-10-23 01:00Z → 02:00Z**). This is a one-off,

not a change to Friday's weekly shows. See [tonight's runbook](docs/DJUKE-ROLLOUT.md#tonights-songs-awaiting-your-vote-runbook).

Only eligible music with known all-time human **0 up AND 0 down** is selected,
including site and Discord votes; 1 up/1 down, adverts and unapproved submissions
are excluded. The full catalog is snapshotted and shuffled when the hour begins.
Songs voted on before their turn are skipped; songs already playing finish.
The order/progress survives restart. Empty/exhausted pools use normal rotation.
Live/Top10 take precedence. Paid DJuke requests wait until the hour ends;
ordinary DeVert breaks continue. Both the site and Discord invite **up OR down** votes.

## Bring A Track

**New here? Start with one song.** Post audio or MP4 in [#DecentJukebox](https://discord.gg/SCtcBggHPa), or click the guitar case on the site. Discord attachments can be up to 10 MB. The site accepts files up to 50 MB, or an existing IPFS file CID for larger media. You do not need a Pinata account.

After a Discord upload is pinned, the bot replies with a **Request NFT** button. Click it to provide your Base artist wallet and optional artwork; submitting the private form automatically adds the request to the owner mint queue. For the site guitar case, connect your artist wallet, enter the track details, and submit. Neither flow mints automatically; the owner reviews and approves requests.

The site's creator briefcase is a three-part flow: drop audio/MP4 video (or paste
a pinned file CID), add title/artist and optional artwork, then review earning
wallets. Local media is detected from its content and previewed without
autoplay; there is no manual format selector or MP3 fallback for unknown files.
Pinned media uses `GET /api/ipfs/media-type?cid=...`, which normalizes the CID
and reads bounded 64 KiB header/tail samples rather than downloading the whole
file. Detection failures are shown explicitly. Artwork accepts an image upload
or a file CID independently of the main media source.

Check **This is a DVert advertisement** for ad submissions. Approval marks the
NFT and recording as an advert, excluded from ordinary music rotation, music
Top 10 and DJuke song registration. Advertisers still book and fund airtime
through DVert separately; this checkbox does not create a paid campaign.

For songs, add up to nine collaborator wallets alongside the artist. Adding or
removing a collaborator defaults the shares to an even split (10000 basis
points, with deterministic rounding); each share can be edited to two decimal
places and the total must be exactly 100%. Duplicate/zero wallets and zero
shares are rejected. These are **DJuke creator-earnings shares only**, not
ownership of a wallet or multiple NFT recipients. The artist still receives
the NFT, ERC-2981 royalties and weekly radio prizes; direct tips still go to
the specified tip wallet. Shares are signed by the submitter, checked server
side, checkpointed with the request, shown during owner approval and included
in minted metadata. DJuke registration and its manifest use the approved
shares; existing registered/requested on-chain splits are never silently
rewritten. A conflicting registration logs an explicit admin-review warning.
Resubmitting the same recording with changed shares or advert classification
requires owner review instead of silently returning the old settings.

### Editing collaborators on an existing song

Open a song card and choose **Add collaborator / split payments**, or open
**Profile → My NFTs**, search for a song, and choose **Collaborators & payments**
beside its title. Both paths open the same editor, labeled with the song title,
NFT token (when available), and DJuke song ID. The song editor is separate from
album creation; no album is needed to add a collaborator.

Total earnings, Song collaborators & payments, and Albums & default payments
use the same compact profile dropdowns as My NFTs, with padded content when
expanded. Selecting a song opens its collaborator dropdown automatically.

The poster links directly to `?tutorial=splits`, a seven-card white-rabbit
walkthrough of standalone-song collaborator edits. It opens the actual Profile
modal, My NFTs dropdown, song editor, approvals section and Admin NFT Requests
panel, with the bunny and spotlight beside each subject. Loaded song settings
are preserved; when no song or request is loaded, disabled, labeled examples
use the existing editor and approval markup in place. Panel controls are inert
during the walkthrough; no wallet connection, signature, proposal, purchase or
payment change is triggered. Leaving restores panel visibility, dropdown state,
scroll and interactivity, and removes all examples. Its progress and completion are
independent of the general and playlist tours. Leave hides it until refresh;
an incomplete linked guide resumes its furthest card, even if the general tour
is complete. A completed linked guide stays hidden until explicitly replayed
using **About → Collaborators & payments guide**.

If older NFT metadata lacks a DJuke song ID, the editor matches the recording's
exact IPFS CID against the configured deployment's public DJuke catalog, then
checks the recording and current splits on-chain. Missing, ambiguous, mismatched,
or unavailable registrations produce an explicit error rather than a guessed
song or an editable empty split. The app targets the deployed v0.5.
Opening an editor alone does not mean approvals or payments have changed.

The header reuses DecentHead's compatible menu/wallet components at MIT-licensed
commit `7baa1c8c47ee33a2162b4dbd4570a14108a24d53`, rather than tracking mutable
`main`. App-specific menu controls and the shared app wallet state remain local.
This release builds on production commit `be3fb9b`, preserving its existing
`purchaseDjukeSong` in `js/djuke-payment.mjs`, live-show and playlist flows.
Approval persistence reuses `createPinataStateStore`; no shared package or new
contract is required for standalone-song edits on v0.5. Album migration and
inheritance changes below remain gated on the undeployed v0.6 candidate.

Split proposals preflight `GET /api/creator/split-status` against the configured
chain and contract before requesting a wallet signature. A current payee's
proposal signature counts as their approval; newly added recipients do not

approve. A sole current payee therefore produces a ready owner-queue request
immediately. Other current payees use the public app's `?splitProposal=…` link
and **Review and approve**, with no gas. The owner rechecks approval status,
expiry, and the live split before applying `configureSong`; reconciliation
requires a confirmed on-chain result. Proposals persist in a dedicated Pinata
checkpoint and expire after seven days.

Release order: deploy the matching worker, verify `/api/creator/split-status`,
then use the matching published frontend. Production authenticated APIs do not
allow arbitrary localhost origins; use the public app for real signatures.

Enter wallet/ENS, role, and percentage in each row. The total must be exactly
100%, with 1–16 distinct nonzero wallets. Choose **Review changes** to resolve
names and compare current and proposed payments. Editing any row invalidates
that review. Create an approval request only after reviewing. Current payees
approve through the shared link, then the admin applies the song change
on-chain. Creating an approval request does not change payments. Credits and
these shares affect DJuke artist payouts, not NFT ownership or ERC-2981 royalties.

The v0.6 candidate treats an untouched single-payee song as using the album
default when it joins an album, after that payee approves migration. Existing
multi-payee or explicitly configured song splits stay custom, even if their
percentages happen to match the album default. New default changes update only
inheriting songs, with current album-payee approvals. A song-specific update on
v0.6 makes an album track custom; v0.5 cannot do that without removing album
membership. Whole-album artist proceeds on v0.6 are divided equally by track
(the last track receives the integer rounding remainder), then distributed
using each track's current split. Requests already purchased retain their
on-chain payment snapshot.

This UI/worker work and v0.6 remain uncommitted release candidates. Deploy the
matching worker routes and coordinate the app's contract address/version before
attempting paid end-to-end validation. Do not point this interface at v0.5 and
expect v0.6 album inheritance behavior.

Deploy the updated worker before publishing the redesigned briefcase: it needs
the media-detection endpoint and signature support for creator splits.

Artwork is optional. Attach PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF up to 10 MB, enter an IPFS image CID for a larger image, or leave it blank to use your Discord profile image. The owner reviews the request and mints approved NFTs directly to the artist wallet.

For Discord NFT requests, including `/jukebox submit` with a media CID, the profile image is queued as the default artwork. Admin shows that image in the preview; leave both replacement fields empty to keep it, choose a new image up to 10 MB, or enter an image/GIF file CID for larger artwork. CID mode references the existing file rather than re-uploading it. A valid CID is not a guarantee of availability; review the image preview before minting. Website-only submissions have no Discord profile association.

## Earn From Radio Plays

Use the same Base wallet for your music NFT and artist payout. A qualifying play is a completed, audible Discord playback of at least 30 seconds. Likes and dislikes influence rotation; they are not paid plays.

Playback rewards are paid only from a funded weekly USDC budget. The owner reviews the completed week's allocation before paying on Base. **Playback Tally counts activity; it does not guarantee a payout.** If no budget is funded or approved, no playback payment is due.

## Help Without Coding

You can help without writing code:

- **Make or share art:** offer original cover art, posters, or video assets. Artists can attach optional cover art to a mint request. For art used across the project, open an issue first and say how we may use it. Only share work you made or have permission to share.
- **Help shape a gallery:** suggest an artist spotlight, a themed listening playlist, or a way to show community artwork in the archive. A broader gallery is an idea to shape, not a separate paid feature today.
- **Test and welcome people:** listen to JukeLoop, vote, test the site on mobile, report a reproducible problem, invite an artist, or host a listening session.

These activities are welcome, but are **not automatically paid**. If you want payment for a specific art, testing, or outreach task, ask the maintainer to agree on the task and bounty before starting. The work must have an eligible GitHub issue and accepted submission to enter repo payroll.

## Build And Earn

1. [Choose an open issue](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentBusking/issues) and ask to be assigned. If you are new to the project, start with a small issue and ask questions.
2. Work on it and open a pull request that includes `Closes #issue-number`.
3. Use the bounty amount and token shown on the issue, for example `bounty: 10 USDC` or `bounty: 10 ART`. Do not guess an amount or add a payout label yourself.
4. After the pull request is merged, an issue with an approved bounty label can enter the repo payout queue. The owner reviews and settles eligible rewards from the funded Base treasury.

Contributor payouts are separate from radio playback rewards. See [Contributor Payroll](docs/PAYROLL.md) and the [Contributor Request form](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentBusking/issues/new?template=whitelist-request.yml) to add your payout wallet. Participating is free; rewards depend on an approved bounty, an accepted merged contribution, and a funded treasury.

## Owner Mint Queue

The contract owner opens **Admin** from the DecentBusking header menu, connects the `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` wallet on Base, and signs to load pending community requests. The queue shows the artist, destination wallet, track, and submitted artwork. Owners can mint requests one at a time or select several for batch processing in groups of up to 20.

New owner-approved mints use DecentNFT v0.3 and require one Base confirmation per batch. The owner wallet pays gas; each NFT is minted directly to its approved artist recipient. Existing v0.2 NFTs remain unchanged and continue to appear in the archive. After confirmation, the bot verifies the collection-qualified Base receipt, updates the durable queue, and announces the minted NFTs in Discord. Reviewed album imports are queued for owner review but never minted automatically.

## DecentNFT On Base

Existing DecentBusking music NFTs use the DecentNFT v0.2 ERC-1155 contract on Base Mainnet:

- Contract: [`0xe63EC9f8228720bAAC2fD528C0A6d06B3Dc5439B`](https://basescan.org/address/0xe63EC9f8228720bAAC2fD528C0A6d06B3Dc5439B)
- Network: [Base Mainnet](https://basescan.org/)
- Metadata and audio: IPFS, pinned through the DecentBusking service
- Artwork: optional IPFS image included in the NFT metadata
- Current royalty: 5% ERC-2981 royalty receiver set to the artist wallet

New owner-approved mints use the deployed DecentNFT v0.3 batch-capable collection. The v0.2 collection remains in the archive; v0.3 does not migrate or renumber existing v0.2 NFTs.

Minted music appears in the DecentBusking 3D timeline and archive for listening and selection. Marketplace purchase, resale, and richer multi-artist royalty splits are still being developed; a DecentMarket link does not necessarily mean a track is currently listed for sale.

The archive initially loads the latest 25 music NFTs. Search the full indexed
archive by artist or song title, select an artist to browse their collection,
or use **Load 25 more** and the timeline to explore older mints. There is no

automatic full-collection download. Admin reviews mint requests in pages of 20.
Deploy the worker's `/api/nfts` and paginated mint-queue API before publishing
the updated browser. A worker cold start may show an explicit catalog-restoring
message until its first verified Base scan finishes.

## How It Works

- **JukeLoop:** Discord voice radio plays community tracks and applies vote-weighted rotation.

# Decent Busking Whitepaper

**A digital town square for music, direct artist support, and accountable community radio.**

Version 0.4 | 10 October 2026 | Implementation-grounded working document

This paper describes the current DecentBusking implementation and its intended development direction. It is not an independent security audit, a rights licence, a token offering, or a promise of investment returns. Features marked as planned are not available merely because they appear here. Configuration and deployed software can change; source files and on-chain records should be checked when making operational decisions.

## 1. Executive Summary

Decent Busking brings the social experience of busking into a web-native listening space: artists share music, listeners discover and support performers, and community radio keeps the archive in circulation. The website combines a three-dimensional music NFT timeline, individual recording playback, a synchronized radio player, direct wallet tips, and public activity tallies. Discord provides the community's upload channel and voice-radio venue.

The project uses Web3 selectively. Base records music tokens and treasury payments. IPFS gives media and metadata content-addressed references. Wallets provide artist destinations and authorize transactions. These tools make important records inspectable and portable; they do not make every part of the service decentralized or confer copyright through token ownership.

The current platform is a **hybrid, owner-operated system**, not a permissionless minting network or autonomous royalty distributor. A Discord bot and Render service manage playback, observations, uploads, and reconciliation. The owner approves NFT requests and authorizes funded payroll. The aim is to make these responsibilities visible rather than obscure them behind decentralization claims.

Artists can receive music NFTs at their chosen Base wallets and direct ETH tips without a platform deduction in the implemented tipping path. Eligible community activity may be included in owner-reviewed payments from funded allocations. Neither uploading, minting, voting, nor accumulating plays guarantees income. The development priority is a transparent, understandable system that gives participants informed choices about public sharing and financial actions.

## 2. Problem And Design Principles

Physical busking connects a performer to nearby listeners, but reach is constrained by place and time. Digital publishing expands that reach while often separating the recording, audience relationship, discovery process, and payment record across different services. A small independent artist may have difficulty knowing how a track was discovered, what activity was recorded, and whether a payment actually happened.

Decent Busking does not claim to remove all intermediaries. It combines familiar community tools with independently inspectable payment and media references to reduce those information gaps.

The design principles are:

- **Listen before transacting.** Exploring the website and listening do not require a wallet or payment.
- **Artist-directed support.** The direct-tip path sends the entered native-token amount to the selected recipient wallet.
- **Separate facts from promises.** Plays, votes, payout proposals, confirmed transfers, and copyright permissions are different records.
- **Make authority visible.** Owner approval, server operations, gateway dependence, and treasury roles must be disclosed.
- **Preserve history.** New weekly counters must not erase lifetime totals; resumed payment queues must not repay confirmed work references.
- **Use bounded budgets.** Payments require reviewed recipients, sufficient funds, and wallet authorization rather than assumed future revenue.

The value of Web3 here is verifiable transaction settlement and content-addressed references, not a guarantee of censorship resistance, permanent availability, legal ownership, or low fees in every circumstance.

## 3. The Ecosystem

### Three Connected Surfaces

| Surface | Current purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **DecentBusking** | Browser experience for radio, a music NFT timeline/archive, song details, direct tips, submissions, and public/personal tallies. |
| **#DecentJukebox** | Discord channel for community media uploads and bot-assisted NFT requests. |
| **JukeLoop** | Continuous, rating-weighted community playback in Discord voice, with synchronized playback on the website. |

### Artist Submission And Archive

The site accepts supported audio and MP4 files up to 50 MB, or an existing IPFS file CID. The Discord attachment flow is bounded at 10 MB. Artwork is optional. Site submissions and explicit NFT requests enter an owner-review queue; they do not automatically mint. Discord ingestion and radio discovery are separate from the NFT-request step.

Discord NFT requests, including media-CID submissions, default to a pinned copy of the uploader's Discord profile image; animated profile images are retained when available. Admin previews the queued artwork and can replace it with PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF up to 10 MB or an existing image/GIF file CID with no attachment-size cap. CID selection references an already-uploaded file rather than uploading it again; parsing the CID does not guarantee its image type, gateway availability, pin retention, or efficient rendering. Native file selectors cannot be prefilled with a profile image, so the preview shows the default separately. Website-only submissions do not establish a Discord identity and cannot infer its profile image.

For approved requests, the owner registers a DecentNFT product and mints an edition directly to the chosen artist wallet. The archive reads minted tokens and their metadata from Base/IPFS. The current mint workflow uses separate registration and mint transactions, not an atomic multi-artist mint batch. MP4 playback is audio-only in Discord voice; the site can display synchronized video.

The guitar case opens submissions; the hat opens tipping. The Left Ankh exposes the public Playback Tally, while the Right Ankh's My Playbacks opens the connected artist wallet's tally. Owner-only Admin and Payroll controls are distinct from ordinary listener tools.

### Audience Participation

Discord reactions and website votes update a shared track tally. Repeated Discord count snapshots apply their delta rather than adding the same observations again. Website votes are limited per browser and active play. Ratings affect rotation, but public browser identities are not proof of unique humans. A fold-away public Top 10 Songs drawer ranks individual songs by New York-week net votes and highlights the live song. The same song ranking determines prize places, with live USDC estimates from the unreserved weekly prize budget.

A qualified playback event requires at least 30 audible seconds of completed Discord playback and an idempotent play identifier. New payout buckets close Monday at 00:00 in `America/New_York`, with daylight-saving transitions handled by timezone data. Previous UTC buckets and all-time totals remain intact. New York accounting starts at deployment; its first week is labelled partial rather than inventing timestamp detail for old UTC aggregates. A new week starts at zero without deleting old buckets. Historical recovery can restore conservative lifetime totals without manufacturing past weekly prize eligibility.

### Submission And Data Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Artist[Artist: site or Discord] --> Upload[File upload or existing file CID]
    Upload --> IPFS[Public IPFS: media and artwork]
```

The radio is not a browser-to-browser peer-to-peer streaming protocol. Discord voice and HTTPS IPFS gateways are part of the delivery path. Pinata is the current production upload/pinning provider; Lighthouse is not an implemented storage layer.

### Payment Proof Flow

The worker's public `GET /api/payroll/ledger` endpoint exposes payment records, verification state, scan coverage, and the latest IPFS snapshot URI. Browser-confirmed payouts can be submitted immediately for independent reconciliation. The worker checks successful Base receipts, canonical block hashes, two confirmations, and the exact router `PayrollPaid` event in DecentBusking's repository namespace.

The comparator runs every 15 seconds, using bounded scan chunks and rotating proof checks. Open Payroll/Admin panels refresh shared status every five seconds. JukeLoop radio state advertises the ledger endpoint. Separate DJuke/DBusk consumers must explicitly integrate it; no unknown external service or token contract is changed automatically.

An explicit historical start block or restored checkpoint determines scan coverage. Without either, discovery begins 2,000 blocks behind startup head. This is not a complete lifetime audit claim. Older known hashes can be reconciled directly. RPC, network, and service failures can delay convergence; the system does not promise instantaneous finality.

## 5. Economics And Payment Mechanics

### Direct Tips

The implemented hat flow sends **native ETH on Base** directly from the connected listener wallet to the selected recipient. It does not route that tip through the payroll contract or deduct a platform fee. The sender separately pays network gas. This statement describes the current code path, not a promise that all external marketplaces or future payment routes are fee-free.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Listener[Listener wallet] -->|Native ETH tip amount| Artist[Selected artist or tip wallet]
    Listener -->|Separate transaction fee| Network[Base network]
```

The user must check the destination and amount. A wallet broadcast is not the same as a successful receipt; the transaction link is the source for confirmation. The current direct-tip handler is not a general ERC-20 tipping implementation.

### Separate Fund Allocations

The shared router uses distinct DecentBusking funds: `dbusk-playback`, `dbusk-top10`, and `dbusk-repo-dev`. An authorized router admin can create a custom purpose fund using a slug-derived ID and public IPFS purpose metadata. Creating a fund does not deposit funds, enable payouts, or attach that fund to a new reward policy.

The USDC deposit workflow checks the configured owner, network, asset, fund activity, token balance, and allowance. It requests an approval for the intended deposit rather than an unlimited allowance when approval is needed. Approval and deposit are separate transactions; depositing into a fund is not an artist payment.

The owner-only recovery control calls the deployed router's `recoverFund` to return a selected amount of remaining native Base USDC to the configured owner wallet. It requires router admin permission, checks actual/fund balances, preflights the transaction, and verifies exact `FundRecovered` and USDC `Transfer` events. Unresolved operations remain locally locked until receipt review. Recovery can work while paused or inactive, but can reduce funding for unpaid proposals. This is not wallet-equivalent custody or a refund of already-paid money.

### Playback And Top 10 Payments

Playback drafts group eligible qualified weekly plays by verified artist wallet and distribute the selected USDC budget proportionally in integer token units. Each artist's provisional share is rounded down. Shares below the chosen minimum and rounding remainder stay unallocated in the fund; they do not automatically become artist debt.

New Top 10 allocations rank individual songs by positive weekly net votes: upvotes minus downvotes. Ties use qualified plays, then title and track ID, matching the public chart. Up to ten songs receive prizes: first takes half the available weekly budget, each subsequent song takes half the remainder, and the final payable song takes all remaining units. Every prize must exceed $0.10; when another half would fall below that threshold, the last payable place takes the remainder instead. A pot of $0.10 or less stays unallocated. One artist may win with multiple songs, paid to the linked artist wallet using a distinct replay-protection reference for each song. Sponsorship and advertising funding change current estimates; Monday midnight in America/New_York freezes the closed-week allocation. Lifetime votes and historical backfill are not retroactively assigned to a prize week. Older artist-based receipts retain their original amounts and replay-protection identities.

After a New York week closes, the running worker automatically prepares IPFS allocation receipts and a retained schedule checkpoint. The default policy offers 100% of unreserved funds, a 0.01 USDC payout minimum, and a warning when average provisional shares are below 1 USDC. Policy values live in `payroll-assets.json`. Budgets are capped by verified closing-block balances and current unreserved money, so later deposits cannot retroactively enlarge an old week. Unpaid receipts are reserved in service accounting; this is not an enforceable on-chain escrow reservation. RPC/IPFS failures stop preparation rather than producing payable guesses. A stopped or sleeping service catches up when running again; there is no guaranteed exact-second execution.

The owner reviews the prepared recipients and amounts, approves missing recipients separately, and authorizes each payout. No server signing key or automatic transfer is introduced. Existing UTC receipts remain importable; payments with overlapping legacy paid references require manual reconciliation. The dashboard and My Playbacks display current fund balances, estimated artist/song contributions and warnings, not debt or a claimable balance. Current multi-artist batches are resumable sequences of wallet transactions; the router's `payoutBatch` groups multiple work items for one recipient, not many artists in one transaction.

Work-reference replay protection skips confirmed payments when resuming the same receipt. It does not freeze a station-wide weekly budget on-chain or prevent the owner from authorizing different new recipients across conflicting receipts. The original reviewed receipt should be retained throughout partial settlement.

### Repository Contributor Rewards

Approved GitHub bounty work can enter a separate repo-dev queue after a qualifying merge or testing approval. Configured payout labels include ART and USDC. The issue, contributor, role, currency, and work reference determine the entry; informal participation is not automatically paid.

The owner-only Settle Payroll workflow verifies the exact Base fund, asset, recipient, amount, work reference, repository, and contributor before modifying queue/account files. Automatic worker dispatch requires a server-only owner credential, `PAYROLL_GITHUB_TOKEN`; otherwise the verified workflow is manual. GitHub commit completion takes workflow time and is not near-instantaneous.

### No Assumed Token Launch Or Guaranteed Yield

The current public configuration does not define a new DJuke/DBusk token issuance, distribution schedule, governance allocation, exchange listing, or redeemable reward balance. ART is a configured repo payout asset, not evidence of a new DecentBusking token launch. Future token proposals would need separate specifications, review, and deployment evidence.

Artist tips, treasury contributions, and grants are different flows. Tips are directed to the selected wallet; they do not automatically finance the platform. Project funding must be explicitly allocated for hosting, IPFS persistence, development, or reviewed artist budgets. Sustainability is a funding and service-design objective, not promised appreciation or passive income.

## 6. Artist Rights And Public Storage

IPFS storage and minting first do not, by themselves, transfer copyright. NFT ownership does not establish ownership of the underlying recording, composition, or other music rights. Separate permissions may be needed for covers, artwork, samples, and performances. Participants should share only material they have the right to share.

The upload form's information notice explains that approved playlist tracks may enter radio, but the current form has no separate recorded radio-consent or opt-out control. An artist who does not want radio playback should contact the administrators before submitting. The notice is information, not a signed licence or consent record.

The notice grants no AI-training or unrelated-reuse permission. That legal distinction is not a technical anti-scraping mechanism: public IPFS files can be downloaded and pinned by others. An artist can request that administrators stop future playlist use or unpin a controlled copy, but the project cannot guarantee deletion of third-party copies or immutable NFT records.

The configured music royalty is a 5% ERC-2981 royalty receiver directed to the artist wallet. ERC-2981 communicates royalty information to compatible marketplaces; it does not guarantee that every sale will pay royalties. Token ownership, royalty settings, and copyright permissions must not be conflated.

## 7. Trust, Security, And Operational Limits

### What Is Independently Checkable

- NFT token and transaction records on Base, with metadata/media CIDs referenced by the archive.
- Successful router payment events, exact token-unit amounts, recipients, fund IDs, and work references.
- Content-addressed copies of allocation receipts, playlist checkpoints, and payment snapshots.
- Versioned source code and GitHub ledger changes.

### What Still Requires Trust

- The bot's interpretation of audible playback, Discord reactions, and browser voting activity.
- Operator decisions about artist review, radio programming, eligible recipients, budgets, and wallet identity associations.
- Availability of Discord, Render, RPC providers, gateways, and pinning services.
- Key custody, correct role assignment, and owner-authorized transactions.

Chain proofs verify payments; they do not independently prove the honesty of the play-count observer or the uniqueness of voters. Anonymous voting remains susceptible to manipulation. No governance DAO or autonomous distribution mechanism is claimed.

The private mint queue requires owner authorization and reconciles existing Base mints before returning requests. It fails closed when metadata cannot be verified, reducing duplicate-mint risk but potentially causing slow loads during RPC/gateway problems. UI visibility alone is not an authorization boundary.

Payment snapshots are retained separately from the recent playlist-checkpoint retention policy. Restored payment records are compared against chain evidence before being labelled verified. IPFS backup failure is a pending-backup condition, not an unpaid bill; retrying persistence must not resend funds.

Reorganizations, provider outages, lost browser-local recovery journals, malicious links, mistaken destinations, smart-contract defects, and wallet compromise remain material risks. Two confirmations are an operational threshold, not a guarantee against all reorganizations. No independent audit or perfect protection is asserted by this document.

previously open drawers and any visible briefcase draft are restored. Finish any
pending submission, close other dialogs, and return from VertLoop to main radio
before starting. Reduced-motion settings keep the rabbit and Mercury still.
The card count sits beside **Follow the White Rabbit**. A centered hole in the
card is the rabbit's home: it dives down, emerges beside the highlighted feature
with a short hop and sparkles, and returns home before the next card appears.
Navigation pauses briefly during the trip; **Leave tour** and **Close tutorial**
remain available. Outside clicks and Escape do not dismiss the tour.
Reduced motion skips the trip and decorative effects.
After completing every stop, the landing-page button is hidden in that browser.
Leaving early does not count as completion. Click **DBusker** to open **About**
and use the identical **Follow the white rabbit** button to replay the tour.
Music notes and little sound-wave rings accompany Mercury's arrivals. These are
visual effects, not extra audio over the radio.

### Build a DJuke playlist with the bunny

[Open the playlist tutorial](https://thejollylama.github.io/DecentBusking/?tutorial=playlists).
This link opens directly to the playlist card even if you have already completed
the general tour. The same card is included after DJuke in the full walkthrough.
Mercury follows the bunny between the real controls:

1. Search for a song or creator and choose a song.
2. Use **Add selected song** to build a draft of up to 24 songs.
3. Name the mix, reorder with **↑ / ↓**, or remove a song with **×**.
4. **Save to Profile** signs and keeps a named revision, without buying playback.
5. **Personal Play** buys your mix at creator prices for your ears only.
6. **Play Live** queues it for the community, at the displayed radio tier prices
   plus $3 per started group of 12 songs. Base network gas is additional.

Protected hours/shows can set your mix aside; remaining songs return to the
   queue afterward without another payment.
   There is no refund solely for that delay or interruption. Separate
   failed-delivery refunds still apply; exact playback times are not guaranteed.
   If your estimated playlist/current/queued playback overlaps a protected block
   on the public calendar, checkout names the show and asks before proceeding.
   Unknown song lengths use a rough four-minute-per-song allowance; ordinary
   checkout without a detected overlap has no separate confirmation window.
7. See how song payments split 90% to musicians/collaborators, 8% to pinning, and
   2% to development, while the separate radio fee splits 25% each to Playback,
   Top 10, Pinners, and Development. The radio fee settles after full delivery.
8. See a labeled illustration of your playlist taking the radio stage after the
   current song and protected shows. Main paid requests can cut in between songs.

**Follow** and **Back** move through these hops without editing your draft,
signing, paying, or changing the live radio. Empty/unavailable controls stay
disabled. The fee-flow and radio illustrations are explanations, not payment
receipts or a live takeover. Ending this linked guide leaves DJuke open to try;
leaving early restores the original drawer and playlist disclosure state.

## Three Names, One Community

| Name | What you are looking at |
| --- | --- |
| **DecentBusking** | The website: live radio, the music NFT archive, artist tips, submissions, and playback tallies. |
| **#DecentJukebox** | The Discord channel where artists post songs and the bot handles upload and NFT-request replies. |
| **JukeLoop** | The ongoing community radio rotation in Discord voice, synchronized to the website's radio. |

An NFT is a token referring to a song and its metadata. Owning or minting the token does not, by itself, transfer copyright or grant music-use rights.

## 1. Listen First

![DecentBusking header, music space, and radio controls](../img/newcomer-listen.png)

Look at the **bottom radio bar**. It shows the current song and artist when JukeLoop is playing.

The screenshot shows the first-load view while the archive and radio are loading. Song artwork and the current track will change; a star field alone does not mean you need to connect a wallet.

1. Click **Tune in** if it appears. Browsers can require a click before sound starts.
2. Use the **speaker button** to mute or unmute, and the **volume control** beside it to adjust the radio.
3. If you see a between-tracks or reconnecting message, wait for the next track. Repeated clicks will not manufacture a live stream.

**You have reached this step when:** you can hear the current track and recognize its title and artist. No wallet or payment is required.

## 2. Vote On What Is Playing

Click **thumbs up** or **thumbs down** in the bottom radio bar while a track is active. Disabled voting buttons mean there is no eligible current play yet. The site accepts one vote per browser for that play, not a new vote for every click.

Votes influence the radio rotation. New Top 10 prize drafts use weekly net votes, but prizes need a funded budget and owner review. A vote is not a payment or a guarantee of earnings.

**You have reached this step when:** the vote control acknowledges your choice.

## 3. Meet A Song And Its Artist

Select a music NFT in the **3D music space / archive**. Inspect its song details and artwork. Click **Preview** for a free 30-second taste or **Listen** to play the whole song. Selecting an archive recording is different from listening to the live radio: use **Radio** in the bottom bar to return to JukeLoop.

Click **Archive** near the upper-right of the music space for the song list, or use **Search Artist or Song** below the header. Wait for metadata to load if the archive is initially empty.

The **hat** opens the tip form. A tip is a real wallet payment, not a free interaction. Check the destination, token, amount, network, and wallet fees before confirming. You do not need to send a tip to keep exploring.

The **Left Ankh** at the top opens the public **Playback Tally**. This is the whole station's activity, not just your songs. Admin and Payroll entries are owner tools; ordinary listeners do not need them.

**You have reached this step when:** you can tell the difference between an archive song, the live radio, and the public tally.

## 4. Bring One Song

![The Submit Your Busk form and its information button](../img/newcomer-submit.png)

Choose one route. Do not submit the same song twice just because owner review takes time.

### Website Route

1. Click the **briefcase** to open **Bring your sound**.
2. Click the little **i** beside the heading and read **Your Music & Public Uploads** before choosing a file.
3. Connect your artist wallet using the **wallet control at the top-right**, then return to the briefcase. Artist actions use Base.
4. Enter the **Title** and **Artist / creator**. Drop supported audio or MP4 up to 50 MB, or choose **Already on IPFS** for an already-pinned file. A CID is not a folder path or a gateway URL; media format is detected automatically.
5. Artwork is optional and accepts an image file or IPFS CID independently of the media source. Check the artist wallet: that is where the approved NFT will go. Collaborator percentages apply only to DJuke creator earnings, not joint NFT ownership, royalties, weekly prizes, or tips. The alternate tip wallet is under the extra options. Referencing another token does not grant permission to use someone else's song. Mark DVert submissions as adverts; airtime is booked separately through DVert.
6. Click **Submit for Approval**. Wallet signatures authorize the upload/submission; read each prompt. This is not the owner's mint transaction.
7. Look for **Queued for owner approval** and the IPFS CID. Keep the CID and wait for review rather than repeatedly submitting.

**You have reached this step when:** the form says the song is queued. The artist request does not mint automatically, promise radio scheduling, or guarantee a payout. The owner reviews and pays gas for an approved mint sent to the chosen artist wallet.

The NFT's royalty setting describes a royalty request to compatible marketplaces, not guaranteed income or copyright ownership.

### Discord Route

1. [Join Discord](https://discord.gg/SCtcBggHPa) and open **#DecentJukebox**.
2. Post one supported audio or MP4 attachment, up to 10 MB for this bot's attachment flow.
3. Read the bot reply and click **Request NFT** when offered. Enter your Base artist wallet and optional artwork as prompted.
4. Wait for owner review and the mint confirmation reply. Discord upload/playback and an NFT request are distinct steps; ask the admins before posting if you do not want your song played on radio.

To hear the Discord radio, join the **JukeLoop voice channel**. If an attachment is too large, use the website's upload or existing-file-CID route instead.

## Public Uploads: Know The Limits

![The upload rights and public storage notice](../img/newcomer-policy.png)

IPFS files can be downloaded, copied, and pinned by others. The information notice grants no AI-training permission, but cannot stop third-party scraping or guarantee that all public copies can be removed. The current form has no separate radio-consent or opt-out checkbox. If you do not want radio playback, contact the admins before submitting.

You can request that we stop future playlist playback or unpin our copy; that does not guarantee erasing other people's copies or immutable NFT records. This notice is information, not a signed licence or consent agreement. Share only material you have the right to share.

## 5. Find Your Own Songs And Counts

1. Connect the **same artist wallet used to receive your music NFT**.
2. Click the **Right Ankh** at the top-right of the title.
3. Choose **My Playbacks**. This opens **My Playback Tally**, filtered to the connected artist wallet.
4. Start with **All Time**, then choose a UTC week to inspect qualified weekly plays. Use song, artist, and upload-date filters to narrow the list.

The song rows show **Plays**, **Likes**, and **Dislikes**. Those like/dislike columns are lifetime totals even when you select a week. Playback payroll uses qualified weekly plays; Top 10 prize calculations separately use new weekly net-vote buckets. Weekly buckets start fresh on Monday UTC while lifetime totals remain.

**You have reached this step when:** you can find your own song and distinguish its lifetime activity from the selected week's qualified plays. If the list is empty, check the wallet, the date/search filters, and **All Time** first. Counts are not a withdrawable balance; owner-reviewed payments need a funded budget.

## When Something Does Not Match

If you cannot hear the radio, check **Tune in**, mute, volume, and whether a track is actually live. If an upload is queued, wait for the owner rather than re-uploading. If a song or NFT is missing, keep the CID, artist wallet, and any confirmation transaction link, then [ask the admins on Discord](https://discord.gg/SCtcBggHPa). Never send anyone your seed phrase or private key.

You now know the loop: **artist shares a song -> owner reviews an NFT request -> approved music appears in the archive and may join radio -> listeners hear and vote -> tallies record activity -> funded, reviewed payouts are a separate step.**
